title: No live self-view while learning
statement: Keep a live view of the learner's own face out of a lesson, because seeing oneself can raise appearance anxiety and lower recall.
example: Across 3 experiments with university students, self-view raised appearance anxiety, and that anxiety lowered lecture recall.
detail: The Grade 9 idea research reports a peer-reviewed paper of 3 experiments with 171, 124 and 224 university students in which camera-on with self-view raised social appearance anxiety most, and that anxiety, not camera status itself, mediated lower lecture recall. It concludes that an audio-only lesson with no camera removes this failure mode rather than designing around it.
against: The study's sample was university students, so applying it to 14- and 15-year-olds is an inference; and a 2021 study by Austin, Fogler and Daniel reports in its title that seeing self and others on screen does not negatively impact learning in virtual classrooms (https://doi.org/10.1037/stl0000303).

evidence.quote: 3 experiments, 171/124/224 university students. Camera-on with self-view raised social appearance anxiety most; that anxiety, not camera status itself, mediated lower lecture recall.
An audio-only, no-camera format structurally removes this failure mode rather than needing to design around it.

citations.ref: Tien, Imundo & Bjork 2023, Viewing oneself during synchronous online learning increases appearance anxiety and decreases memory for lecture content, Applied Cognitive Psychology
Austin, Fogler & Daniel 2021, Seeing self and others on-screen does not negatively impact learning in virtual classrooms, Scholarship of Teaching and Learning in Psychology
